subject: Re: Aurora - proposed SLA baseline amendment and monthly credit scaling
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@auroradata.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@auroradata.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: SLA baseline ask — regional uplift / monthly credit approach

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement reviewed the standard SLA and we have two asks before we can circulate to our finance/legal teams: 1) a regional baseline in EU with a slightly lower uptime commitment tied to our traffic profile, and 2) a monthly credit cap that scales by usage tier rather than a flat percentage.

Specific asks:
- EU regional baseline: propose 99.6% (instead of the 99.9% global baseline) for a subset of endpoints handled in our Frankfurt region — Aurora will accept the slightly lower uptime in exchange for lowered unit cost for EU traffic.
- Monthly credit structure: we’d like a tiered cap that maxes out at 6% of the monthly invoice for our entry tier, 4% for mid usage, and 2% for high-usage committed tiers. We want this expressed as a deterministic formula so finance can model cashflow.

Attached is a short procurement note with suggested wording (see attached). Can your commercial/legal team review and propose language we can redline? If useful, happy to set a 30‑minute sync next week.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Procurement, Aurora Data
elaine.park@auroradata.com

Attachments: procurement_sla_note.docx (referenced)

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@auroradata.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA baseline ask — regional uplift / monthly credit approach

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear note and the proposed caps. Looping in Ben (sales) and Aditya (legal/product) to scope how we can express the tiered cap cleanly in the SLA.

Quick responses:
- We can offer a region-specific baseline at 99.6% for traffic pinned to the EU region, provided Aurora commits to the traffic segmentation and any cross-region failover is handled as an exception.
- Tiered monthly credit caps are workable, but we typically anchor caps as a percentage of the monthly invoice (so finance can model). We’ll draft a formula that references 'monthly billable usage' and the three bands you suggested.

I’ve attached an initial redline from our side (Aurora_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf) capturing the EU baseline language, scheduled maintenance carve-ins, and a first pass at the tiered cap calc.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call Thursday 28th at 10:00am ET to walk the redline and agree on the exact formula. If that works for you, I’ll send calendar invite.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Partner Sales — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachments: Aurora_SLA_Redline_v1.pdf

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@auroradata.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 08:17:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA baseline ask — regional uplift / monthly credit approach

Elaine — appreciate the clear bands. A few practical points from commercial:
- We can accept the 99.6% EU baseline for endpoints pinned to the region, but we’ll need the region pinning defined in an annex (routing rules + how Aurora will label traffic for invoicing).
- Proposed cap ladder (commercial):
  * Entry tier (monthly usage < $50k): cap = min(6% of bill, $25k)
  * Mid tier ($50k–$250k): cap = min(4% of bill, $50k)
  * Committed tier (>$250k): cap = min(2% of bill, $100k)
This hybrid percent + hard-cap protects both parties on extremely large invoices. I attached an example spreadsheet with modeled scenarios.

If that approach looks reasonable, we’ll put it into the SLA language and highlight where the hard-cap numbers can be negotiated in the term sheet.

Thanks,
Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: aurora_usage_tiers.xlsx

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@auroradata.com>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:44:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aurora - proposed SLA baseline amendment and monthly credit scaling

Elaine / team — I reviewed Markus' redline and Ben's commercial ladder. A few legal/ops comments to incorporate:
1) Maintenance carve-ins: we propose scheduled maintenance windows (up to 8 hours/month for platform upgrades) be excluded from uptime calculation provided customers receive 72-hour rolling notice and have an opt-out if they need an avoidance window per quarter.
2) Latency SLO: uptime alone doesn't capture user experience for your latency-sensitive endpoints. We recommend adding a latency objective (p50/p95) for pinned endpoints; failure of latency SLO triggers a separate credit schedule (smaller percentages but more frequent).
3) Credit calculation formula (draft language):
   credit = max(percentage_cap * monthly_invoice, raw_credit_by_uptime_bucket)
   where percentage_cap is based on the usage band and raw_credit_by_uptime_bucket is the standard remedy table tied to measured downtime minutes.
4) Monitoring & audit: Aurora must accept Redwood's telemetry as primary for credit calculations; we'll include a 10-business-day window to dispute telemetry with log exports and retain a joint incident review within 30 days.

I will push these items into the next redline. If Aurora prefers alternate monitoring precedence (their telemetry primary), we can negotiate an escrowed measurement approach but that will add complexity to dispute resolution language.

—Aditya
Head of Product Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@auroradata.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 14:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Aurora - proposed SLA baseline amendment and monthly credit scaling

Team — thanks for the rapid turn. We reviewed the redline and Ben's hybrid ladder; the proposal is close. Two follow-ups before we can sign: 1) can you confirm final credit calculation example for August (low‑traffic month) and November (peak) with numbers plugged in so finance can reconcile, and 2) can the scheduled maintenance exclusion be limited to a 6‑hour monthly allowance for EU‑pinned endpoints?

We’re okay with Redwood telemetry as primary provided Redwood publishes the incident report and raw uptime minute buckets each month. Also please confirm whether latency SLO credits are additive or carve into the monthly cap (we prefer they be additive, but can accept carve-in if the cap increases slightly).

If you can send a final sample calculation and updated redline with the 6‑hour carve-in alternative, I can route for final procurement sign-off. Otherwise happy to take the 30‑minute call if that helps.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Procurement, Aurora Data
elaine.park@auroradata.com
